# Setup for comparison

The below scripts are setup to compare a specific release to the current
version in use. E.g. loaded in R-Studio. (SBoo and SBooScripts). This
can be a release, e.g. the tag or specific branches in SBoo and
SBooScripts.

```{R Specify temporary directory, include = FALSE}
# Specify where the downloaded versions of sboo and sbooscripts should be saved to
dest_folder <- "SimpleBox"
```

## Define function for downloading and ordering the folders needed to compare

```{R Switch to SBoo release 2026.3.1 branch, results ="hide", echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("vignettes/Development/Quality control/ComparisonFunctions.R")
folderpaths <- CompareFilesPrep(Release = NA,
                                devBranch = "development",
                                Test_SBoo = "verctorfunc",
                                Test_SBooScripts = "SB2dplyrDAG",
                                Temp_Folder = dest_folder)
```

Select random substances for testing

```{R select substances, results ="hide", echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
excluded_substances <- c("Graphene Oxide", "Chitosan", "nTiO2_P25_CaLIBRAte_D6_3", "nAg_NanoFase", "nanoparticle", "GO-Chitosan", "PET_sphere_example")

microplastics <- c("TRWP", "microplastic_fiber", "microplastic_cube", "microplastic_sphere", "microplastic_ellipsoid", "microplastic_particle", "microplastic_fiber_elips", "microplastic")

substances <- read.csv("data/Substances.csv")

# Select 5 random substances for each class from substances csv
# and always select the default microplastic.
set.seed(492)

mp <- substances |>
  filter(Substance %in% microplastics) |>
    slice_sample(n = 5, replace = FALSE) 

substances <- substances |>
  filter(!Substance %in% microplastics) |>
  filter(!Substance %in% excluded_substances) |>
  group_by(ChemClass) |>
  slice_sample(n = 5, replace = FALSE) |>
  ungroup()

substances <- rbind(substances, mp) |>
  distinct()
```

# Compare default version of SBoo

## Calculate for test version

Calculate first order rate constants for the other version. Here we
apply the new initWorldOther from the current branch as there are
missing links to the new install folder in the old release. This can be
changed in future comparisons.

```{R}
setwd("SimpleBox/SBtest/SBooScripts")

use_local_sboo = TRUE
use_scenario_data = FALSE
```

```{R}
SBInstallFolder <- "SimpleBox/SBtest" 
```

```{R}
source("baseScripts/csv_to_json.R")

# Calculate the kaas 
other_kaas <- data.frame()

substances <- read.csv("data/Substances.csv") |>
  filter(ChemClass == "particle" | Substance == "default substance")

selected_substances = c("microplastic", "nAg_10nm", "nZnO", "default substance")

substances <- substances |>
  filter(Substance %in% selected_substances)
  
for(substance in substances$Substance){
  type = substances |>
    filter(Substance == substance) |>
    pull(ChemClass)
  
  if(type != "particle"){
    type = "molecule"
  }
  
  csv_to_json(substance_name  = substance, 
            data_path = "data", 
            type = type) 
}

substance_jsons <- list.files("data/custom_jsons")

file = substance_jsons[3]
for(file in substance_jsons){
  devtools::load_all("../SBoo/")
  SBooDataLocation = "data"
  #World <- sboo::SBcore$new(SBooDataLocation, SuBmode = file.path("custom_jsons", file), debugR = F)
  
  World <- sboo::SBcore$new(SBooDataLocation, SuBmode = "substance_data_nano.json", debugR = F)
  
  AllF <- ls("package:sboo") %>% sapply(FUN = get)
  
  World$UpdateKaas()
  
  substance_name <- sub("^substance_data_(.*)\\.json$", "\\1", file)

  other_kaas <- rbind(other_kaas,  World$kaas |>
    mutate(Substance = substance_name,
           ChemClass = World$fetchData("ChemClass")))
}
```

## Calculate for most recently published version

Calculate the first order rate constants for the current branch

```{R Clean environment again, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls()[sapply(ls(), function(x) is.function(get(x)))])
```

```{R Run SB and get advection ks for FLux_work branch, results ="hide", echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
setwd("../../../SimpleBox/SBmain/SBooScripts")

current_kaas <- data.frame()
  
for(substance in selected_substances){

  source("baseScripts/initWorld.R")
    
  current_kaas <- rbind(current_kaas,  World$kaas |>
                          mutate(Substance = substance,
                                 ChemClass = World$fetchData("ChemClass")))
}
```

## Compare scales, compartments and species present
Because of the new implementation of the states and species, we will first check
if the same scale-species-compartment combinations are present in the new version
as in the old version. 

### Check number of rows
```{R}
# Check the length of the dataframes 
nrow(current_kaas)
nrow(other_kaas)

# Check compartments present at scales 
other_scale_compartments <- other_kaas |>
  select(from.SubCompart, to.SubCompart, from.Scale, to.Scale) |>
  rename(fromSubCompart = from.SubCompart,
         toSubCompart = to.SubCompart, 
         fromScale = from.Scale, 
         toScale = to.Scale) |>
  distinct()

current_scale_compartments <- current_kaas |>
  select(fromSubCompart, toSubCompart, fromScale, toScale) |>
  distinct()

by_cols <- c("fromSubCompart", "toSubCompart", "fromScale", "toScale")

only_in_other <- other_scale_compartments %>%
  anti_join(current_scale_compartments, by = by_cols)

only_in_current <- current_scale_compartments %>%
  anti_join(other_scale_compartments, by = by_cols)

# There are differences. Fix states and see which differences remain






# There are 210 rows less in the other_kaas dataframe. 
current_kaas_no_0 <- current_kaas |>
  filter(k != 0) 

other_kaas_no_0 <- other_kaas |>
  filter(k != 0)

# When all zeros are removed, we have the same number of rows in both dataframes. This means there were 0s in the current version that could have been removed. This difference should not have yielded different results. 

# Now check for NAs: 
current_kaas_no_NA <- current_kaas |>
  filter(!is.na(k)) 

other_kaas_no_NA <- other_kaas |>
  filter(!is.na(k))
```

### Missing states

The code below shows that the only missing processes in the new implementation of
SBoo are processes that should not be in the matrix anyways; the Unbound processes
for particulate species. 

```{R}
common_cols <- setdiff(intersect(colnames(current_kaas), colnames(other_kaas)), "k")

check_states <- merge(
  other_kaas,
  current_kaas,
  by = common_cols,
  suffixes = c("_Old", "_New"),
  all = TRUE   
)

missing_states <- check_states |>
  filter(is.na(k_Old) | is.na(k_New))
```

## Compare rate constants, k's.
The code below shows there are no changes between the two versions of SBoo, 
which is what we would expect. Just to be sure we will check the differences in
steady state masses in the next chunk.

```{R Calculate the differences between ks, results ="hide", echo=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
common_cols <- setdiff(intersect(colnames(current_kaas), colnames(other_kaas)), "k")

kaas_comparison <- merge(other_kaas, current_kaas, by=common_cols, suffixes = c("_Old", "_New"))

kaas_comparison <- kaas_comparison |>
  mutate(diff = k_New-k_Old) |> # If this number is positive, the New_k is higher than the Old_k (higher advection rate with new method)
  mutate(rel_diff = diff/k_New)

changed_kaas_all <- kaas_comparison |>
  filter(diff != 0) |>
  mutate(full_name = paste0("From ", fromSpecies, "_",fromSubCompart, "_", fromScale, 
                            " to ", toSpecies, "_", toSubCompart, "_", toScale))

head(changed_kaas_all)

unique(changed_kaas_all$process)

changed_kaas <- changed_kaas_all |>
  filter(abs(rel_diff) > 0.001) 

unique(changed_kaas$process)
```

# Compare the remove global scenario 
In the dplyr version of SBoo, the method of defining specific scenarios (changing scales, subcompartments, species) 
has changed. Below we will show how this is done for the scenario that was used by Saadi et al. (2027). 
In this scenario, the global scale is removed and the deepocean compartment is introduced at the Regional and
Continental scales. 

## Step 1: Change the StateRules.csv
The StateRules.csv can be found in SBooScripts/data, and contains any exceptions
that SBoo has to take into account regarding scales, subcomparts and species. There
are 3 rules in this file that are used for the default World, and we will alter this 
file to fit our scenario. 

```{R}
setwd("../../SBtest/SBooScripts")

staterules <- read.csv("data/StateRules.csv")

# Remove the second rule which disallows deepocean at regional and continental scale
staterules <- staterules |>
  filter(SubCompart != "deepocean")

# Alter the first rule to remove all compartments at the global scales
staterules <- staterules |>
  mutate(SubCompart = case_when(
    Scale == "Tropic,Arctic,Moderate" ~ "naturalsoil,agriculturalsoil,othersoil,river," 
  ))

```

```{R}
setwd("../../SBtest/SBooScripts")

staterules <- read.csv("data/StateRules.csv")

# Alter the first rule to remove all compartments at the global scales
staterules <- staterules |>
  mutate(SubCompart = case_when(
    Scale == "Tropic,Arctic,Moderate" ~ "agriculturalsoil,othersoil,river,lake,freshwatersediment,lakesediment" 
  ))
```
